Waterfall Routes for Motorcycle Tourers

Britain's wet climate creates some spectacular waterfalls, and many of the best are on or near great motorcycle roads. These routes combine thrilling riding with the chance to stretch your legs at some of nature's most dramatic displays of power and beauty.

Scotland's Waterfall Roads

  • Falls of Measach (Corrieshalloch Gorge): On the A832 near Ullapool. A short walk from the car park to a Victorian suspension bridge spanning a 200ft gorge with a thundering waterfall below. Spectacular and easy to access.
  • Steall Falls, Glen Nevis: Park at the end of the Glen Nevis road and walk 45 minutes through a dramatic gorge to reach Steall Falls — a 120m cascade that's one of Scotland's finest. The ride through Glen Nevis is stunning in itself.
  • Falls of Shin, Sutherland: On the NC500 route near Lairg. Famous for Atlantic salmon leaping the falls. The car park is right beside the road.
  • Grey Mare's Tail, Dumfries & Galloway: On the A708 between Moffat and Selkirk — one of Scotland's best riding roads. The waterfall is visible from the road and a short walk takes you to the base.

Wales's Waterfall Country

The Brecon Beacons contain a designated "Waterfall Country" (Fforest Fawr) with multiple falls accessible from riding roads:

  • Sgwd yr Eira (Waterfall of the Snow): Near Pontneddfechan. Unique because you can walk behind the curtain of water. Park at the village car park and walk 30 minutes along a riverside path.
  • Sgwd Clun-Gwyn: The tallest in Waterfall Country at 15m. Accessible from the same walking routes.
  • Pistyll Rhaeadr, Powys: The tallest single-drop waterfall in Wales at 73m (240ft). Accessible by a narrow road from the B4396. The ride through the Berwyn Mountains to reach it is superb.
  • Swallow Falls, Betws-y-Coed: Right beside the A5 in Snowdonia. A small entry fee gives access to viewing platforms over this powerful series of cascades.

England's Best Waterfall Rides

  • High Force, Teesdale: England's largest waterfall by volume. On the B6277, one of the finest riding roads in the North Pennines. A short walk from the car park takes you to this powerful cascade on the River Tees.
  • Aira Force, Lake District: Near Ullswater on the A592. A 20m waterfall in a wooded gorge. The ride along Ullswater to get there is one of the Lake District's finest roads.
  • Hardraw Force, Yorkshire Dales: England's highest single-drop waterfall. Access is through the Green Dragon pub in Hardraw — buy a drink and walk through the pub garden to the falls.
  • Janet's Foss, Malhamdale: A beautiful woodland waterfall near the village of Malham. Combine with a ride over the Pennines via the Settle-Carlisle road.
Waterfalls are at their most impressive after rain — which in the UK means they're impressive most of the time. But heavy rain makes the access paths slippery, so wear proper footwear. Your motorcycle boots may be fine for short walks, but ankle-deep mud in leather boots isn't fun.

Planning a Waterfall Tour

  • Most waterfalls require a short walk from parking — 5 to 45 minutes typically
  • Wear boots suitable for wet, uneven paths
  • Carry a waterproof for your camera/phone — spray from falls reaches further than you'd expect
  • Visit after rain for maximum flow (but check for flood warnings)
  • Combine waterfalls with nearby riding roads for a day ride with purpose

Waterfall stops break up a riding day perfectly. They get you off the bike, stretch your legs, and reconnect you with the raw natural power that makes British landscapes so extraordinary. keyTakeaways: Waterfalls are at their most powerful after rain, which in Britain means most of the time.
Scotland's Falls of Measach and Falls of Shin sit right beside the road, while Steall Falls needs a 45-minute walk.
The Brecon Beacons' Waterfall Country includes Sgwd yr Eira, where you can walk behind the curtain of water.
High Force in Teesdale is England's largest waterfall by volume, on the superb B6277.
Wear proper footwear for slippery paths and carry a waterproof cover for your camera or phone.

faq.q: When are the waterfalls most impressive?
faq.a: After heavy rain, when flow is at its fiercest, which given the British climate is much of the year. Autumn and winter usually deliver the biggest cascades, while a dry summer spell can reduce even Pistyll Rhaeadr to a trickle. Check for flood warnings after prolonged downpours, because access paths beside rivers can become dangerous when levels surge.

faq.q: What footwear should I bring for waterfall walks?
faq.a: Bring boots or shoes suitable for wet, uneven, and often muddy paths. Motorcycle boots cope with short roadside walks such as the Falls of Measach, but the 45-minute route to Steall Falls or the riverside path to Sgwd yr Eira calls for proper grip. Spray from the larger falls reaches further than you expect, so pack a waterproof for your camera.

faq.q: Which waterfall is best for a quick roadside stop?
faq.a: Pistyll Rhaeadr is essentially roadside once you reach it, and the Falls of Shin near Lairg has a car park right beside the NC500 route. High Force in Teesdale and Aira Force by Ullswater need only a short walk from parking. These suit riders wanting to break up a day without committing to a long hike in riding gear.

faq.q: Can I walk behind any of these waterfalls?
faq.a: Yes, Sgwd yr Eira in the Brecon Beacons Waterfall Country is famous for it: a path leads behind the curtain of falling water. Park at the village car park near Pontneddfechan and follow the riverside path for around 30 minutes. Expect the ground to be slippery and prepare to get lightly soaked, so protect anything you do not want wet.
